title: Justificare in Scripture usually forensic: declare just, not make just
source_text: I. Justificare, quod est Hebraice hitsdik, Graece dikaioo, in Scriptura sacra sumitur plerunque sensu forensi, id est, non significat ex injusto justum facere, sed justum declarare, habere, agnoscere illum qui fuerat alicujus criminis, vel culpae accusatus, aut vocatus in suspicionem.
pass_a_gloss: To justify, which is in Hebrew hitsdik, in Greek dikaioo, is taken in sacred Scripture for the most part in a forensic sense: that is, it does not signify to make a just man out of an unjust one, but to declare, hold, and acknowledge as just him who had been accused of some crime or fault, or called into suspicion.
pass_b_english: Justificare (Heb. hitsdik, Gk. dikaioo) is usually forensic in Scripture.
It means declaring or acknowledging as just the one accused—not making the unjust just.
